question: Should OpenClaw adopt the RFC’s centralized localization runtime and process-wide localized operator presentation as a core five-PR foundation, rather than continue with surface-specific localization only?
rationale: This introduces a new shared package, a broader environment-driven presentation behavior, generated governance checks, and cross-surface contracts; choosing their permanent scope is product and architecture direction rather than a mechanical review fix.

options.title: Sponsor the staged foundation
options.body: Approve the central runtime direction, require serial rebases after the foundation slice lands, and resolve the shared Gateway/UI boundary before reviewing the later bundles.

options.title: Narrow to existing surfaces
options.body: Keep the current localized UI and wizard paths, then split any narrowly justified CLI or updater localization into independently reviewable changes.

options.title: Pause the RFC series
options.body: Defer the shared runtime until maintainers define supported locales, compatibility guarantees, and ownership for the new cross-surface contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the staged foundation
recommendation.body: Approve the central runtime direction, require serial rebases after the foundation slice lands, and resolve the shared Gateway/UI boundary before reviewing the later bundles.
